newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel says ITT seeks okay to sell some shares.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel says ITT seeks okay to sell some shares.

text.p: ITT Corp has approached French engineering firm Alcatel Alsthom to ask for permission to sell some Alcatel shares before a shareholders' pact expires on July 3, an Alcatel spokesman said Wednesday.
He was responding to a Reuters query after ITT rejected a takeover bid from Hilton Hotels Corp on Wednesday and indicated it was considering selling non-core assets.
"They (ITT) have approached Alcatel to ask for authorisation to be able to sell some shares before July 3," the Alcatel spokesman said. He declined further comment.
It was not clear when the approach had been made.
ITT signed a shareholders' agreement with Alcatel in 1992, pledging to retain its shareholding until July 3, 1997.
Last April, however, it was able to sell 2.1 million of the 9.4 million Alcatel shares, which it then held to a U.S. investment fund with Alcatel's approval.
ITT now controls around five percent of the French electrical engineering and telecommunications group and the 1992 shareholders' agreement remains in force, Alcatel sources say.
